title: a markup literal takes `<?= expr ?>` as a hole for any expression
scope:
the second hole a markup literal has, what it accepts, and what a `<?nvs` tag inside a
literal is. It does not touch double-quoted strings or heredocs, whose `{$…}` grammar stays PHP's,
and it does not change what a hole's value goes through at the sink, which is [0169](0169.md)'s.
dependsOnText: [0169](0169.md) for the literal and its `{$…}` holes.
validatedBy:
`tests/conformance/core/an-html-template-takes-an-output-tag-hole-for-any-expression.nvst`
and the reject cases beside it.
